meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'без-' ('without, -less') (stem 'ответственный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('irresponsible').

examples.trans: When we act irresponsibly...

examples.text: Это был очень безответственный поступок с твоей стороны.
examples.trans: That was a very irresponsible act on your part.

examples.text: Шеф не терпит безответственных людей на своей кухне.
examples.trans: The chef does not tolerate irresponsible people in his kitchen.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'thanks to' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: And it is all thanks to you.
It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Но благодаря вам у нас все получилось. Спасибо вам за вас.
examples.trans: But thanks to you, we made it work. Thank you for being you.

meanings.note: Comparative: ближе. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('close, near').

examples.trans: We have grown closer.
This is my close friend.

examples.text: Слушайте, Марина, мы с вами стали ближе!
examples.trans: Listen, Marina, the two of us have grown closer!

meanings.note: Comparative of много. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.
Comparative of большой. Core Russian adv meaning 'more' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.
I don't need any more.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'бояться собак'. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be afraid (of), to fear'.

examples.trans: We have nobody to fear here.
I'm not afraid.

examples.text: Это наш город. Нам здесь бояться некого.
examples.trans: This is our town. We have nobody to fear here.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'conclusion' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Из этой неприятной истории каждый повар должен сделать правильный вывод.
examples.trans: From this unpleasant story every cook must draw the right conclusion.

examples.text: Шеф быстро пришёл к выводу, что соус нужно готовить заново.
examples.trans: The chef quickly came to the conclusion that the sauce needs to be made anew.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.

examples.trans: What are you doing?
I'm making dinner.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.
He's my friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.trans: Could we go somewhere else?
That's a different building.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to win, to conquer', paired with 'завоевать'.

examples.trans: It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Именно благодаря качеству мы завоёвываем уважение гостей.
examples.trans: It is precisely thanks to quality that we win the respect of guests.

examples.text: Талантливый повар быстро завоёвывает авторитет на кухне.
examples.trans: A talented cook quickly wins authority in the kitchen.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: вот именно = that's just it, quite right
А именно = namely. Core Russian part meaning 'exactly, namely, precisely' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Exactly, quite right.

examples.text: Именно это я и хотел сказать.
examples.trans: That is justamente what I wanted to say.

examples.text: Вот именно. Но мне сдаваться нельзя.
examples.trans: Exactly. But I must not give up.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.
I'm going to Mum's.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: It needs a wash.
We need to do even more.
It needs a wash!

meanings.note: + dative of the person, + accusative of the drink

examples.trans: Are you pouring me vodka?
Mum is pouring tea.

examples.text: Ты мне сейчас водку наливаешь, да?
examples.trans: Right now you're pouring me vodka, aren't you?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'one', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нам очень дорого обходится авторская кухня.
examples.trans: Auteur cuisine costs us very dearly.

examples.text: Это все, кто выходил из отеля.
examples.trans: That is everyone who left the hotel.
What is going on here right now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: под мою ответственность = on my responsibility

examples.trans: It's my responsibility.
On my personal responsibility.

examples.text: Хорошо, давайте три. Под мою личную ответственность.
examples.trans: All right, let's say three. On my personal responsibility.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'метить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to celebrate, to note', paired with 'отмечать'.

examples.trans: But we should celebrate that.
We need to celebrate this.

examples.text: Я хотел отметить день рождения вместе.
examples.trans: I wanted to celebrate the birthday together.

meanings.note: Пить чай = to drink tea. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to drink', paired with 'выпить'.
used on its own: он пьёт = he drinks

examples.trans: I'm drinking tea.
He doesn't drink.

examples.text: Всё, теперь ты герой? И можно только пить?
examples.trans: So now you're a hero? And all you have to do is drink?

related.gloss: to go on a drinking binge

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Deliberate act of a person. Common masculine noun meaning 'act, action, deed' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I committed a very foolish act.

examples.text: Это был благородный и смелый поступок.
examples.trans: It was a noble and brave deed.

examples.text: Соколов, не делай сейчас таких глупых поступков.
examples.trans: Sokolov, do not do such foolish deeds right now.

meanings.note: Qualitative adjective. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('correct, right, proper').

examples.trans: A course of the correct antibiotics.
That is the correct answer.
We have prescribed a course of the correct antibiotics.

meanings.note: 'на работе' = at work. Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'work, job' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'm going to work.
There's a lot of work.
I'm at work.

meanings.note: + infinitive: решил стать = decided to become
Решить задачу. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to decide; to solve', paired with 'решать'.

examples.trans: The court has decided.
I've decided.

examples.text: Суд решил: домашний арест по месту прописки.
examples.trans: The court has decided: house arrest at his registered address.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.en: to commit an act or make a mistake
meanings.note: Transitive verb. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to commit, make (mistake)', paired with 'совершить'.

examples.trans: You are making a huge mistake.

You are making a huge mistake, Stepanych!

становиться.gloss: to become, to get, to grow

meanings.note: + instrumental. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to become, to get, to grow', paired with 'стать'.

examples.trans: And you are becoming an alcoholic.
And you are becoming an alcoholic. Goodbye!
It is getting very cold outside.

meanings.note: с другой стороны = on the other hand
Common feminine noun meaning 'side' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: On the other hand, it's interesting.
The shop is on that side.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange, odd').

examples.trans: She's really strange.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Lyolya will definitely come!

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

meanings.note: Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'respect' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It is what earns us respect.

examples.text: Именно благодаря честному труду мы завоёвываем уважение гостей.
examples.trans: It is precisely through honest work that we earn the respect of guests.

examples.text: На этой кухне каждый повар пользуется заслуженным уважением.
examples.trans: In this kitchen every cook enjoys well-deserved respect.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'thing; piece' in everyday Russian.
Common feminine noun meaning 'thing; piece' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Life is a complicated thing.

examples.text: А жизнь — сложная штука. Вы понимаете, о чём я?
examples.trans: And life is a complicated thing. Do you understand what I am talking about?
And life is a complicated thing.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
